clues.title: Language: Serbian
text: There are three versions of the Serbo-Croatian language recognized in Bosnia and Herzegovina: Bosnian, Serbian and Croatian. Speakers consider them separate languages though, and base the split on the ethnicity of the user: Bosniak, Serb or Croat. Serbian (and Bosnian technically ) use either Latin or Cyrillic, while Croatian always uses the Latin script. In practice, it is **only** in Serbian-majority regions (mostly in Republika Srpska) where you will find Cyrillic.
NOTE: Serbian is **also** commonly written with Latin script, and thus might be indistinguishable from Bosnian/Croatian.
ALSO NOTE: Official road signs may use both scripts **nation-wide**.
The Serbo-Croatian word for street is **улица**/**ulica** (like most Slavic languages).
